podcast.title: Beggars Group Collective
podcast.body: Now known as the Beggars Group, the company has expanded exponentially to become a central "solar system" of affiliated labels. This group includes Matador, Rough Trade, XL Recordings, and Young Turks, featuring a roster of artists like Radiohead, Jack White, The Strokes, Queens of the Stone Age, and Adele. "The Bigger's group, as it's now called, is the center of a solar system of labels that include Matador, Rough Trade, XL recordings, and Young Turks."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of Indie Rock: Part 2

podcast.title: Founding and Longevity
podcast.body: Beggars Banquet was established in 1977, inspired by the DIY ethos of the original punk rock movement. Unlike many of its contemporary indie labels, Beggars Banquet notably "never, ever went out of business," maintaining continuous operation. "The Beggars banquet provided another key ingredient to the indie record culture in Britain in the 80s."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Origins from Record Stores
podcast.body: Beggars Banquet grew out of a chain of record stores managed by Martin Mills and Nick Austin. The founders deeply embraced the do-it-yourself ethic of punk music, leading them to establish their own indie label. "Baker's banquet grew out of a chain of record stores run by Martin Mills and Nick Austin. They loved the whole do it yourself, ethic of punk, and they bought into the idea 100%."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of Indie Rock: Part 2

podcast.title: Pioneering Independent Label
podcast.body: Beggars Banquet was listed as one of the small independent labels that worked outside the major label system during the rise of indie music. "that included rough trade for a D, beggars banquet, epitaph, SST, and many others."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Post-Punk Explosion Part 7: All the rest

podcast.title: Roster Strategy for Success
podcast.body: Beggars Banquet implemented a carefully curated roster strategy, balancing "fringy stuff" with commercially successful groups to ensure its long-term viability. This approach meant for every artist like The Lurkers or Bauhaus, there was a Gary Numan or The Cult providing financial stability. "They maintained a carefully groomed roster, balancing out the fringy stuff by being just successful enough with a few groups."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Support for Gothic Bands
podcast.body: Beggars Banquet was described as one of the "small nimble indie labels" that regularly appeared in post-punk England, signing artists like Bauhaus and releasing their debut single, "Bela Lugosi's Dead." "Bauhaus and Bella Logosi's dead, at least on beggars banquet, another one of those small nimble indie labels that popped up almost daily in post-punk England."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
